Available unit-hours divided by the hours in the day. Twenty-four out of twenty-four units gives exactly the unit count; with a machine down for half a day it comes out fractional.
The plant declares no unit count, so the system counted the child equipment locations — which include the weather station, and that generates nothing. Declare the real figure and rebuild.

A level for SCANNING BY EYE, not a contract threshold. Every O&M contract commits to a different figure; assessment against the commitment lives in Contracts ▸ Assessment & payment, not here.

One row can be missing several things at once; this field takes the WORST. Without the energy figure, energy availability cannot be computed at all, so it ranks above; with unattributed hours the figure still comes out, it is just not yet known who to charge.

Declared at UNIT LOCATION level. It has to be explicit: on the demo, the shipped curve leaves the component category empty, so the "which curve matches this unit" lookup matched wrongly because empty matches empty — a comparison that returns true with nothing actually being true.

Two figures side by side: availability by time and by energy. They differ, and they differ widely — a turbine down in a windless spell loses almost nothing, while one down in a windy spell loses tens of thousands of kWh.

Declared at PLANT level. At 0 the system counts every child equipment location — and counts wrongly: a weather station is an equipment location too but generates nothing, so a plant with sixteen inverter stations comes out with seventeen units. Availability is then one seventeenth too low while still sitting in a plausible-looking range.
